title: Illness ends his Shaw job; Buddy Rich takes over
summary: Leeman is hospitalized for hemorrhoids and sent home to Maine; Shaw signs Buddy Rich, Glenn Miller calls, and he recalls Chick Webb and Ella next door at the Roseland.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: But to get back to Artie Shaw, I became ill and it was just before Christmas at the Lincoln Hotel, and I had -- well, I don't mind telling you, I had a drummers occupational disease, hemorrhoids, and it was serious.
That's really a pain in the buns, isn't it?
I tell you. I was in the hospital, they took me back to Maine, and Artie Shaw couldn't wait until I got well, so he gave Buddy Rich a contract.
Is that how that dude got in there?
That is how Buddy followed me in that band.

But I was very ill for several months, four or five months. Glenn Miller had called me, and wanted to hire me. He wanted to lead -- Glen / Island Casino, Glenn Miller. He had borrowed money from Sy Schribner man in Boston.
He was at that New England bandstand where all the musicians played.

He had everything. That was our, with Artie Shaw, that was our twice a week, we worked out of the Roseland Ballroom, next door to me which I had missed along the way just then, was next door to us, and Lawarge's Restaurant was Chic Webb, and his wonderful orchestra, and a little 17-year-old girl named Ella Fitzgerald.
